2609.09157.title: Learning Length-Extrapolatable Recurrent Models
2609.09157.paper_summary: Recurrent models provide a natural path to long-context modeling, yet models trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT) often fail beyond their training horizon. Classical analyses emphasize gradients that vanish or explode along temporal paths. However, dense per-token losses can still train a shared recurrent rule despite severe decay, showing that decay alone does not determine whether learning fails. We instead study state credit: the signal through which future losses reach earlier recurrent states before contributing to parameter updates. Accordingly, we intervene directly on state credit and propose Credit Stabilization through Time (CST). During backward propagation, CST locally rescales the state-credit signal to stabilize its norm without rotating the component being corrected, while leaving the forward computation unchanged. Because controlled synthetic tasks and real data exhibit different credit dynamics, we specialize CST to each regime. In both settings, CST improves performance beyond the training horizon, with gains observed at up to 128x the training length.
2609.09157.paper_summary_zh: 重複模型提供了一條自然的長期上下文建模之路，但通過時間反向傳播（BPTT）訓練的模型往往在其訓練範圍之外失敗。傳統分析強調沿著時間路徑消失或爆炸的梯度。然而，儘管衰減嚴重，密集的每個標記損失仍然可以訓練共享的重複規則，顯示僅僅衰減並不決定學習是否失敗。我們改為研究狀態信用：未來損失通過此信號到達早期的重複狀態，然後才對參數更新做出貢獻。因此，我們直接介入狀態信用，並提出了通過時間的信用穩定化（CST）。在反向傳播期間，CST局部重新縮放狀態信用信號，以穩定其範數，而不改變被修正的組件，同時保持前向計算不變。由於受控的合成任務和真實數據顯示出不同的信用動態，我們將CST專門化到每個範疇。在這兩種情況下，CST在訓練範圍之外提高了性能，觀察到的增益可達訓練長度的128倍。
2609.09157.author: Hanwen Jiang et.al.
